% The conversion with wasysym left in place. It renders correctly, compiles clean, is
% tagged, and has NO Missing character in the log -- so C-GLYPH-MISSING's cheap log grep
% does not see this one. What is wrong is the text layer: $\leadsto$ comes back as ";".
%
% amssymb is loaded FIRST here on purpose. wasysym redefines \leadsto, so load order does not
% save you and the source names no wasysym command at all.
%
% ";" is also C-PDFTEX-MATH's signature, so the Step 4 maths-corruption grep fires on this
% file for an entirely different reason. Check the engine before concluding which you have.
%
% Mechanism: wasysym pulls the Type 1 font wasy10 with a Builtin encoding. LuaTeX does emit
% a /ToUnicode CMap for it, but an incomplete one -- veraPDF names the used glyph as code 50
% and the CMap maps only 14 codes, not including it. With no mapping an extractor falls back
% to the raw code byte. Fails PDF/UA-2 clause 8.4.5.8-1.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard={a-4,ua-2}, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}
\usepackage{amssymb}
\usepackage{wasysym}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
\frametitle{Symbol source}
State A $\leadsto$ B done.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
